definitions.explanation: Losing a war. In Japanese, this word most commonly refers to Japan's defeat in World War II, but it can also describe any military defeat or, more broadly, losing in a competition or match.

examples.japanese: {敗戦|はいせん}⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{立|た}ち{直|なお}った→立ち直る：15049_tachinaoru⟧。
examples.english: Japan recovered from its wartime defeat.

examples.japanese: {敗戦|はいせん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{責任|せきにん}→責任：03298_sekinin⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{問|と}う→問う：02299_tou⟧⟦{声|こえ}→声：02207_koe⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{上|あ}がった→上がる：00615_agaru⟧。
examples.english: Voices arose calling for accountability for the defeat.

examples.japanese: {敗戦|はいせん}⟦{直後|ちょくご}→直後：04525_chokugo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{食料|しょくりょう}→食料：03250_shokuryou⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{物資|ぶっし}→物資：07863_busshi⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{不足|ふそく}→不足：03598_fusoku⟧し、{多|おお}く⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{国民|こくみん}→国民：02757_kokumin⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{苦|くる}しい→苦しい：02636_kurushii⟧⟦{生活|せいかつ}→生活：01443_seikatsu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{強|し}いられた→強いる：15604_shiiru⟧。
examples.english: Immediately after the defeat, Japan lacked food and supplies, and many citizens were forced to endure difficult lives.

notes:
USAGE:
When used without further context, {敗戦|はいせん} in Japanese most often refers to Japan's defeat in World War II (1945). The word ⟦{終戦|しゅうせん}→終戦：18973_shuusen⟧ (end of the war) is a more neutral alternative often used officially, while {敗戦|はいせん} explicitly acknowledges defeat. In sports contexts, {敗戦|はいせん} can also mean a loss or defeat in a game.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {敗戦|はいせん}⟦{後|ご}→後：30157_go⟧: after the defeat
- {敗戦|はいせん}{国|こく}: defeated nation
- {敗戦|はいせん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{色|いろ}→色：00849_iro⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{濃|こ}い→濃い：02344_koi⟧: defeat appears imminent (lit. "the color of defeat is thick")

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{終戦|しゅうせん}→終戦：18973_shuusen⟧: end of the war (neutral, avoids the word "defeat")
- ⟦{敗北|はいぼく}→敗北：12872_haiboku⟧: defeat (broader; applies to battles, elections, and competitions)
